headline: Frontend Developer (junior) with 2 years of experience building React‑based products
summary: Junior Frontend Developer specializing in React, TypeScript, and Next.js, currently contributing to a health‑tech product at Docplanner in Warsaw. Previously completed a frontend internship at Allegro, where I delivered reusable UI components and improved test coverage. Skilled at translating Figma designs into performant, accessible code and collaborating closely with product and UX teams.

experience.title: Junior Frontend Developer
highlights: Developed a new patient appointment booking flow using React 18 and TypeScript, raising conversion from 3.4% to 3.8% (+12%) in the first month of A/B testing.
Reduced initial JavaScript bundle size by 28% through dynamic imports and tree‑shifting, lowering payload from 1.2 MB to 860 KB and improving TTI on mid‑tier devices.
Authored 150+ unit and integration tests with Jest and React Testing Library, achieving 92% code coverage and cutting regression bugs reported in QA by 40%.
Implemented Tailwind CSS‑based design system components from Figma specs, decreasing average UI development time per feature from 3 days to 1.5 days.
Mentored two interns on React best practices and Git workflow; their pull requests were merged without senior review after three weeks.

experience.title: Frontend Intern
highlights: Created a reusable product card component in React with TypeScript adopted by five internal micro‑frontends, eliminating roughly 1,200 lines of duplicate code.
Built end‑to‑end checkout tests with Cypress, catching 15 critical bugs pre‑release and reducing post‑release hotfixes by 30%.
Assisted in migrating legacy styles to Tailwind CSS across 12 UI pages, raising internal style‑consistency score from 78% to 94%.
Joined a Scrum team of six engineers, contributing an average of four story points per sprint and participating in sprint planning and retrospectives.
Produced interactive Figma prototypes from stakeholder feedback, shortening design‑to‑development handoff time by roughly 20%.
